hilbert-01.status_headline: Gödel (1938) and Cohen (1963) showed the continuum hypothesis is independent of ZFC; there is no consensus that independence answers Hilbert's question. The well-ordering question is answered yes in ZFC by Zermelo's theorem (1904).
hilbert-01.decided_by: Claude (AI) for the site operator; not yet signed off by a person
hilbert-01.note: Research marked it solved by independence. Wikipedia's Hilbert table lists it as partially resolved and says there is no consensus that independence is a solution, so it is shown as open with the independence results as evidence.

hilbert-09.status_headline: Artin's reciprocity law (1927) answers the abelian case; a general reciprocity law for non-abelian extensions remains open (Langlands program).
hilbert-09.decided_by: Claude (AI) for the site operator; not yet signed off by a person
hilbert-09.note: Research marked it solved under a literal reading. Wikipedia's Hilbert table lists it as unresolved, with Artin reciprocity as a partial result, so it is shown as open; the reading-dependence is marked as an ambiguous statement.

hilbert-13.status_headline: For continuous functions, Hilbert's expected impossibility is false (Kolmogorov 1956, Arnold 1957); the variant for algebraic functions remains open.

hilbert-13.note: Standard formulations state two variants: continuous functions (answered by the Kolmogorov–Arnold theorem) and algebraic functions (open). One stated variant is answered, so partial, matching Wikipedia's 'partially resolved'.
